title: 'Disappointed': San Diego council, mayor at odds over city budget - NewsBreak
text: SAN DIEGO (FOX 5/KUSI) — Several San Diego City Council leaders are reacting to Mayor Todd Gloria’s vetoes to the city’s budget. The mayor brought a budget to city council, and they made revisions to items they believed the community wanting to see, including restoring more libraries and lakes. On Tuesday, they approved the budget with a 7 to 2 vote, ahead of the June 15 deadline. After city council’s approval, the budget went into the hands of Gloria, who announced on Tuesday he was line-item vetoing several of the items put in place by city councilmembers. Now, a majority of the city council and the mayor are at odds. “I’ll be honest, I’m quite disappointed with the vetoes that came through from the mayor,” Councilmember District 7 Representative Kent Lee said. “I’m pretty disappointed with the way the mayor is approaching the budget at this point,” said Councilmember Raul Campillo, who represents district seven. Part of the mayor’s line-item vetoes included cutting recreational programming at lakes, except for at Lake Miramar and Lake Murray, and brush management enforcement, among funding for several other items and positions, that was initially passed by city council on June 10. “We have a strong mayor, a strong council form of government and you see the council exercising its will,” said Vivian Moreno, councilmember for district eight. “I think that the veto as presented would be a real step backward from what the council did last week,” District 9 Councilmember Sean Elo-Rivera said. “I don’t think what the mayor proposed,” Moreno added. “Reflects what I want to see in my city.” “As mayor I cannot in good conscience allow a budget built on shaky assumptions to move forward,” Gloria said in a video announcement when he announced the vetoed items on Tuesday afternoon. Moreno said if she had to pick one item to reinstate from the mayor’s veto, she would say, “It’s between storm water and it’s also between brush management, that’s huge.” “ We’re going to bring back more than that, we need to bring back more than that,” Elo-Rivera said, when asked which one item he believes was of the upmost importance to bring back from the mayor’s vetoes. Council President Joe LaCava’s office has confirmed that he will place an item on Monday’s city council meeting docked for council to consider accepting, or overring the mayor’s vetoes, either whole, or in part. “We advocate, and explain to the public why it’s important for them to show up on Monday and have their voice heard and we explain that restoring the budget as council had passed it is the best way to provide for the wants and needs of San Diegans, it’s responsible, it’s balanced,” Elo-Rivera said. “To be honest I haven’t decided where I’m going to land, obviously I was a No.” Moreno said, referring to her NO vote during the prior budget. “I guess time will tell we kind of have the weekend to mull it over, there’s going to be a lot of communication on my part with my colleagues.” “We’re going to remain responsible and we’re going to do what the community is asking for us and I think that council ultimately has the final say,” Campillo said. The council is expected to take up the veto for consideration on Monday, they can either override the vetoes with a vote of six councilmembers, or sustain it. They have until Thursday to decide, but are expected to vote on Monday. For the latest news, weather, sports, and streaming video, head to FOX 5 San Diego & KUSI News.
